# Bibliography and Additional Resources

This appendix compiles bibliographic references, official tool documentation, and recommended reading cited throughout the course units.

---

## 1. Bibliographic References

*   **Attaran, M. (2017)**. *Cloud computing technology: Leveraging the power of the internet to improve business performance*. Journal of Systems and Information Technology, 19(3/4), 232-254. (Referenced in cloud computing introduction and storage architectures).
*   **Kimball, R., & Ross, M. (2013)**. *The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling*. John Wiley & Sons. (Core reading for Part I: Dimensional Modeling and Star/Snowflake Schemas).
*   **Chapman, P., Clinton, J., Kerber, R., Khabaza, T., Reinartz, T., Shearer, C., & Wirth, R. (2000)**. *CRISP-DM 1.0: Step-by-step data mining guide*. SPSS. (Foundational analytical methodology for Part II).

---

## 2. Official Documentation and Technology Guides

To dive deeper into the practical tools used in course laboratories, consult the following online resources:

*   **Google Cloud Architecture Framework**: Architectural design guides for Google Cloud systems. [View documentation](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework).
*   **BigQuery Quickstart Guide**: Reference documentation for analytical storage and large-scale querying. [View documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs).
*   **PySpark SQL and DataFrame API**: Complete reference for distributed data transformations at scale. [View documentation](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/python/index.html).
*   **dbt (Data Build Tool) Documentation**: Guide for SQL data transformation within the Data Warehouse and orchestration. [View documentation](https://docs.getdbt.com/).

---

## 3. Datasets and Case Studies

*   **TheLook eCommerce Dataset**: Public dataset simulating transactions, users, shipments, and inventory for an online clothing store. Hosted in BigQuery Public Data (`bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce`).
*   **BigMart Sales Prediction**: Retail sales case study used in Part II laboratory modules for predictive modeling and preprocessing.
